summary: Ukrainian air defenses intercepted or suppressed 119 enemy drones during a large-scale overnight attack involving 153 UAVs launched from multiple directions including Bryansk, Orel, Kursk, and occupied territories. Multiple Shahed and Geran-5 drones struck targets across central and western Ukraine, including Ternopil, Vinnytsia, and Kyiv regions, causing casualties and infrastructure damage. Ukrainian forces also reported destroying a key Russian offensive axis in the Siversk direction during Operation Vivaldi.
key_points: Ukrainian air defenses shot down or suppressed 119 of 153 enemy drones during a major overnight attack launched from Bryansk, Orel, Kursk, Millerovo, and occupied Donetsk and Crimea regions (Source: @kpszsu/90340).
Russian strike drones hit Ternopil, killing three and injuring eight including a child, with a high-rise fire and damage to a store and vehicles (Source: @UkraineNow/84879).
A Geran-5 missile struck Ternopil city, confirmed by local monitoring channels (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77538).
Two Geran-5 missiles were detected approaching Kyiv from the north, with one heading toward Rusanivka and Bereznyaky districts (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77505).
Ukrainian military intelligence reportedly disrupted Russian plans to capture Sloviansk and Kramatorsk during Operation Vivaldi (Source: @UkraineNow/84878).
A shooting incident in Kyiv's Sviatoshyn district left one dead and one injured after a conflict escalated with a traumatic weapon (Source: @UkraineNow/84877).
Starlink connectivity remains stable above 400 km/h speeds despite restrictions on offensive drone usage (Source: @UkraineNow/84871).

sections.executive_summary: Ukrainian air defenses intercepted 119 of 153 enemy drones during a coordinated overnight attack involving Shahed, Geran-5, and other UAVs launched from multiple directions. Strikes across Ternopil, Vinnytsia, and Kyiv regions caused civilian casualties and infrastructure damage. Ukrainian forces also claimed to have disrupted a major Russian offensive operation in the Siversk direction.
ukraine: Air defenses engaged a massive drone barrage overnight, shooting down 119 of 153 hostile UAVs including 64 reactive Shaheds, Geran-5 missiles, and decoy drones launched from Bryansk, Orel, Kursk, Millerovo, and occupied territories (Source: @kpszsu/90340).

In Ternopil, Russian drone strikes killed three people and injured eight, including an 11-year-old girl in serious condition, with a high-rise fire and damage to a store and parked cars (Source: @UkraineNow/84879).
A Geran-5 cruise missile struck Ternopil city, confirmed by regional monitoring channels (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77538).
Two Geran-5 missiles were detected approaching Kyiv from the north, with one heading toward the Rusanivka and Bereznyaky districts (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77505).
A reactive drone was tracked flying through the Chernobyl exclusion zone toward western areas (Source: @kpszsu/90366).
In Kyiv's Sviatoshyn district, a street conflict led to a fatal shooting when an individual used a traumatic weapon, resulting in one death and one injury (Source: @UkraineNow/84877).
Starlink services remain operational at speeds exceeding 400 km/h, maintaining stable communication for defense forces (Source: @UkraineNow/84871).
russia: Russia launched a large-scale drone offensive involving 153 UAVs including 92 reactive Shaheds, Geran-5 missiles, and decoy drones from Bryansk, Orel, Kursk, Millerovo, and occupied Donetsk and Crimea regions (Source: @kpszsu/90340).

Russian forces attempted a major offensive operation codenamed Vivaldi targeting Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, which was reportedly disrupted by Ukrainian military intelligence (Source: @UkraineNow/84878).
A high-altitude drone was detected flying from Ivano-Frankivsk toward Zakarpattia at an altitude of 4.4 km (Source: @eRadarrua/126169).
Russian drone activity included coordinated strikes across multiple regions including Vinnytsia, Khmelnytskyi, and Kyiv oblasts (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77525).
The Russian Defense Ministry has not publicly commented on the failed offensive in the Siversk direction (Source: @UkraineNow/84878).
Russian forces continue to deploy Geran-5 cruise missiles in attacks against Ukrainian cities (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77538).
No official Russian military casualties or losses have been reported in connection with these operations (Source: @kpszsu/90340).

sections.threat_assessment: The overnight drone barrage represents a significant escalation in Russian aerial warfare tactics, with coordinated attacks from multiple vectors including occupied territories and distant regions. The use of Geran-5 cruise missiles alongside mass Shahed deployments indicates an intensified campaign targeting Ukraine's civilian infrastructure and urban centers. Ukrainian air defenses demonstrated resilience but faced an unprecedented volume of threats, suggesting Russia may continue escalating attack frequency and complexity. The disruption of Operation Vivaldi shows Ukraine's capability to counter major offensive operations, but the continued drone pressure across all fronts indicates sustained Russian intent to destabilize the country.
sections.regional_response: Ukrainian air defense systems successfully engaged the majority of incoming threats, demonstrating improved interception capabilities against diverse drone types and cruise missiles. Local authorities in affected regions including Ternopil and Kyiv responded to casualties and infrastructure damage, with emergency services addressing fires and structural damage. The government maintained public communication through Telegram channels, providing real-time updates on air alerts and threat status. International partners continue monitoring the situation, with ongoing discussions about additional military aid packages to support Ukraine's air defense capabilities.
sections.intelligence_notes: The coordinated nature of the drone attack from multiple launch points suggests centralized planning and execution by Russian forces, potentially involving elements from the Southern Military District and Aerospace Forces. The inclusion of high-altitude drones flying at 4.4 km indicates advanced operational capabilities and possible testing of new tactics. Ukrainian electronic warfare units played a crucial role in suppressing drone guidance systems, contributing to the high interception rate. The timing of attacks coincided with reduced visibility conditions, suggesting deliberate selection of optimal operational windows. Continued monitoring of Russian drone procurement and deployment patterns is essential for anticipating future attack vectors.
